resources.name: LZR
quotes: We use the open-source scanner LZR [45] to fingerprint unexpected services for 13 of the most popular TCP scanning protocols: HTTP, TLS, SSH, TELNET, SMB, RTSP, SIP, NTP, RDP, ADB, FOX, REDIS and SQL.
references: [45] L. Izhikevich, R. Teixeira, and Z. Durumeric. LZR: Identifying unexpected Internet services. In USENIX Security Symposium, 2021.
resources.used_in_paper_reasoning: The paper uses the LZR scanner to fingerprint unexpected services on popular TCP ports.

resources.name: Censys Universal Internet Dataset
quotes: IP addresses that previously hosted services that were indexed by Shodan [69] or Censys [32] attract a significantly different set of scanners and are targeted by 7 times more exploits than IP addresses that have never hosted search engine indexed services.
we investigate how attackers use the most-frequently scanning Internet service search engines [53]—Censys [32] and Shodan [69]—to find services.
references: [32] Z. Durumeric, D. Adrian, A. Mirian, M. Bailey, and J. A. Halderman. A search engine backed by Internet-wide scanning. In CCS, 2015.
resources.used_in_paper_reasoning: The authors use Censys to identify previously indexed services and to systematically leak services to test attacker behavior.
